classification.difficultyReason: Apply the explicitly taught exponential sketch and y-axis reflection directly for bases 3 and 10, using standard benchmark points.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sketch on one set of axes the graphs of $y=3^x$ and $y=3^{-x}$.

answer.short: Reflections in the $y$-axis, meeting at $(0,1)$; both have asymptote $y=0$.
answer.worked: Plot $y=3^x$ through $(-1,\frac13),(0,1),(1,3)$. Reflect these points in the $y$-axis to obtain $y=3^{-x}$ through $(-1,3),(0,1),(1,\frac13)$. Draw smooth positive curves approaching $y=0$.

spec.description: Reflected base-3 exponentials with shared intercept and guides at x=±1.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Sketch on one set of axes the graphs of $y=10^x$ and $y=10^{-x}$.

answer.short: Reflections in the $y$-axis, meeting at $(0,1)$; both have asymptote $y=0$.
answer.worked: Plot $y=10^x$ through $(-1,\frac1{10}),(0,1),(1,10)$. Reflect these points in the $y$-axis to obtain $y=10^{-x}$ through $(-1,10),(0,1),(1,\frac1{10})$. Draw smooth positive curves approaching $y=0$.

spec.description: Reflected base-10 exponentials with shared intercept and guides at x=±1.
